problem_statement:
fix(epics): harden ingest — skip (no-epic) headings + resolve dep targets (#144)

Two generic footguns in `epics ingest`:

1. Every `## heading` became an epic, so preamble/context sections
   (Symptom, Evidence, Constraints, ...) turned into junk epic rows. Add an
   opt-out marker: a heading ending in `(no-epic)`/`(context)`/`(ignore)` is
   skipped (heading + body). Backward-compatible.

2. Dependency targets were split on whitespace and inserted raw without
   matching a real epic id, so a natural `depends on: Epic 0` produced bogus
   or dropped edges and a silent `0 dep edges`. Now split dep lists on commas
   only and resolve each token to a real epic id (exact -> slug-exact ->
   unique slug-prefix -> unique slug-substring, across parsed + existing
   epics). Unresolved/ambiguous tokens emit a WARNING and are counted as
   skipped in the summary — never silently dropped.

Applied identically to the legacy bash CLI (bin/mini-ork-epics) and the
Python port (mini_ork/ported/mini_ork_epics.py) so the parity test stays
green; adds unit tests for marker-skip, dep resolution, and the
unresolved-warning path.

problem_statement:
fix(plan): repair invalid planner JSON via bounded LLM retry, not a hardcoded plan (#145)

When the planner LLM returned invalid JSON (or a plan missing
verifier_contract.checks), mini-ork silently substituted a deterministic
recipe plan built from workflow.yaml — losing model-authored verifier commands
and degrading planning quality.

Replace that degradation with a bounded LLM repair-retry loop, grounded in the
structured-output / self-repair literature:
- Iterative self-repair (arXiv:2604.10508) + error-reflection prompting
  (arXiv:2508.16729): re-invoke the planner with its raw invalid output + the
  EXACT validation error + an instruction to return ONLY valid JSON restating
  the required schema keys.
- Truncation guard (arXiv:2605.13076 / JSONSchemaBench 2501.10868): detect
  unbalanced-brace truncation (a top cause of invalid JSON) and flag it in the
  repair prompt.

Behavior:
- Recoverable validation failures (parse_error / missing_verifier_contract /
  bad_artifact_contract / bad_node_types) now trigger up to MO_PLAN_MAX_REPAIRS
  (default 2) LLM repair attempts, re-validated each time.
- If repairs are exhausted, planning HARD-FAILS (exit 1, D-015 forensics
  preserved) — Zero-Fallback, never a silent hardcoded plan.
- The old deterministic fallback survives only behind an explicit opt-in
  MO_PLAN_DETERMINISTIC_FALLBACK=1 (default OFF).

Applied identically to the bash CLI (bin/mini-ork-plan) and the Python port
(mini_ork/ported/mini_ork_plan.py) to keep the parity test green; adds tests
for repair-recovery, exhaustion hard-fail, and the deterministic opt-in.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MEQ3iCysDCxmTbvYa8PgMj

problem_statement:
fix(reward): anchor reward_g on verified execution, not the LLM judge (#168)

* research: does agentic SLM distillation work + who ships it + method ranking

arxiv: works bounded (Agent Distillation 2505.17612 = 7B at 93% of 32B teacher;
AFM 2508.13167 7B beats undistilled 32B, 84.6% token cut; TinyAgent 1.1B ~= GPT-4T
on function calling) but fails long-horizon/novel-tools/<=3B capacity. Productized
+ consolidating: OpenPipe ART (ART-E beats o3, ->CoreWeave), Arcee (Agent 7B +
DistillKit + ClawRouter), TensorZero (5-30x). Ranking: RL-from-verifiable-reward >
SFT-distill > multi-agent->SLM > capacity-aligned > on-policy(nascent). For Co-Evolve:
premise de-risked but NOT a moat; use SFT then ART-style RL on verifier rewards.

* research: correct 'who ships it' — Distil Labs is the purest match, not OpenPipe/Arcee

Recovered subagent research corrected two errors: OpenPipe/ART is GRPO RL (not
distillation, pivoted away, ->CoreWeave); Arcee's distillation is generic text
transfer (agentic bolted on). The actual pure-play is Distil Labs (Berlin 2024,
dltHub Agent Distillation Jul 2026): trace-in -> teacher-seeded 10k synthetic ->
compact student -> OpenAI-compatible endpoint, 50-90% cheaper — i.e. TraceOtter's
exact loop, shipped first. Fireworks = biggest agentic cost-savings evidence
(Genspark +33% tool calls/-50% cost) but a side feature. Sharpens Co-Evolve note:
distillation NOT a moat; our edge is whole-agent orchestration + the verifiable
reward ART-style RL needs and we already emit.

* fix(reward): anchor reward_g on verified execution, not the LLM judge

reward_from_status was judge-anchored: verdict="approve" → 1.0 checked BEFORE
execution status. A self-improving loop whose reward is a self-generated judgment
degrades or games itself (arXiv 2510.02840 Goodhart, 2602.10531 collapse-vs-
improvement, 2606.01066 verifier-fuzzing) — and this repo's reviewer is provably
unreliable (false-negatives, theater passing gates).

Reward-chain veto semantics (arXiv 2601.18533): execution status is the PRIMARY
verified anchor; the reviewer verdict may only VETO (downgrade), never fabricate a
positive. Judge-approve + execution-fail = 0.0 (anti-Goodhart). Review-only nodes
(no execution signal) keep the verdict fallback. Bash + python parity + 5 regression
assertions.

This is the code-verified linchpin (Finding 3) that lets a compounding curve be a
real measurement instead of judge-gaming. Produced by mini-ork dogfooding itself:
framework-edit run-1783856585-87239 (verified via real smoke, not the run verdict).
subject: fix(reward): anchor reward_g on verified execution, not the LLM judge (#168)

problem_statement:
fix(plan): stop rejecting JSX/HTML tags as dry-run placeholders (#171)

validate_plan() flagged any string shaped like <...>, recursing into every
nested value. A plan for a React codebase naturally names component tags --
"<ContentNodeCreationModal>" -- and every such plan was rejected as
placeholder_plan. mini-ork could not plan work on ANY React/JSX repository.
It also mis-flagged the planner's own step annotations ("<shell-only>").

A placeholder plan means the planner produced NOTHING: the dry-run stub,
whose objective is "<dry-run: not generated>" and whose decomposition is
empty. So judge the plan by its objective and its emptiness, not by every
string inside it. An angle-bracketed value now only counts as a stub when it
carries a stub word (dry-run / TODO / TBD / FIXME / placeholder / fill-in) or
is empty.

Caught live: a real fix-duplicate-modals run against a React repo died at
plan validation with placeholder_plan while holding a perfectly good plan.
subject: fix(plan): stop rejecting JSX/HTML tags as dry-run placeholders (#171)

problem_statement:
fix(conductor): make the conductor falsifiable + add the dispatch API

THE BUG. conductor_decisions: 10 rows, 10 with predicted_score, ZERO with realized_score.
The conductor predicted a score for every decision it ever made and never once recorded what
it actually got. It was uncalibrated BY CONSTRUCTION — it could not learn from its own
choices, and no UI could answer "was the recommendation right?", because nothing wrote the
answer down. A prediction nobody scores is not a prediction, it is a claim.

WHY the existing write-back never fired: it reconciled only against an EPIC's terminal status.
But `mini-ork run` completes a TASK_RUN and does not necessarily advance any epic — on the
live db all 10 decisions pointed at epic `libwit-se-1`, still marked `not started`. The join
matched nothing, forever. The outcome was unreachable, not merely unwritten.

FIXES
  0050  task_run_id (reconcile against the run, which actually finishes)
        proposed_* + decided_by + override_reason (see below)
  0051  epic_id becomes NULLABLE. It was NOT NULL, which encodes the same wrong assumption:
        a run-driven dispatch has no epic, so recording its decision was IMPOSSIBLE — the
        insert failed and the decision was silently never written. The system kept making
        choices it never recorded, which is how it got uncalibrated in the first place.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN CALIBRATION
proposed_* vs chosen_* + decided_by captures the signal the product was throwing away:

    the system proposed X · a human chose Y · Y turned out better/worse

That is a LABELLED EXAMPLE. Verified live, end to end:
    decided_by=human  proposed=implementer=opus_lens  chosen=implementer=minimax_lens
    outcome=success   realized_score=1.0
That row could not have existed before this commit.

NEW: POST /api/v1/dispatch  — mints the run-id, records proposed-vs-chosen, returns the exact
command + env to spawn. An override is DERIVED from (proposed != chosen), never self-reported,
so the UI cannot lie about it by omission. mini-ork does not spawn the process; the caller does
(Orca's PTY), which is what makes the terminal native and the correlation deterministic.

NEW: GET /api/v1/dispatch/options — the recipes, and what each lane and topology has ACTUALLY
cost and won on THIS repo. Honesty gates enforced server-side, not left to the UI:
  · n < 5 returns evidence="none" and NO rate. Not a dimmed rate — none. If the UI can read a
    number it will render one, and a rendered number gets believed.
  · every rate ships a Wilson interval.
  · predicted_score is deliberately NOT returned: until decisions carry realized_score it is
    unfalsifiable, and that is exactly the kind of figure this project has had to retract.

THREE BUGS IN MY OWN FIX, CAUGHT BY TESTING AGAINST THE REAL SCHEMA
  1. run_id was `run-{epoch}-{hash(kickoff)%100000}` — two dispatches of the same kickoff in
     one second COLLIDED (they'd share a run dir and corrupt each other). It collided on the
     first test. Now secrets.token_hex(4); verified 5/5 unique.
  2. I checked status in ('done','success','pass'). task_runs has a CHECK constraint and NONE
     of those values can occur — the terminal success state is `published`. My unit tests
     passed only because they used the same invented status. The fixture now carries the real
     CHECK constraint so a test CANNOT invent a value production rejects.
  3. I gated on `ended_at IS NOT NULL`. That is not terminal: 8 live rows sit in `reviewing`
     with ended_at set. Now gated on the status set. And `verdict` is empty on 242 of 278
     completed runs, so it is only ever a negative override ('CRASH'), never the positive one.

10 new tests (incl. the exact live situation: a finished run whose epic never moves).
129 passed across the suite, no regressions.
subject: fix(conductor): make the conductor falsifiable + add the dispatch API

problem_statement:
fix(framework-edit): capture the implementer delta, not pre-existing tree dirt (#174)

framework-edit's implementer edits MO_TARGET_CWD in place, and the reviewer diff
was 'git diff' (working tree vs HEAD). With any unrelated uncommitted change
already present — e.g. a CONCURRENT session sharing the working tree — that diff
swept it into review-diff.patch, so the run could review and PUBLISH another
session's work. Deterministic whenever the tree is dirty; hit repeatedly, and a
concurrent session independently worked around it by stashing.

Fix: snapshot the tree BEFORE the implementer runs via a non-destructive
'git stash create' (records current tracked mods as a commit without touching the
tree/index/stash list; empty => clean => baseline is HEAD), persist to
<run_dir>/pre-implementer-ref, and diff against that baseline so only the
implementer's delta survives.

Tests (real throwaway git repo, no mocks): pre-existing dirt in A.txt is excluded
while the implementer's edit to B.txt is captured; clean-tree happy path still
captures; baseline is idempotent across revision loops.
Verified: tests/run-all.sh unit 520/520; pytest 1273 passed / 27 skipped.

problem_statement:
fix(learning): stop the gradient/reward loop confabulating on empty + ungrounded traces

The reflection->gradient loop mined "learned failure modes" from degenerate
control nodes and injected them into planner/researcher/reviewer prompts,
describing an empty run that never happened. Six fixes:

- gradient_extractor: skip zero-work control nodes (no duration/cost/evidence)
  instead of confabulating a defect from them (BUG4a).
- gradient_extractor: feed the extractor whole-run context (node count, roles,
  total cost/duration, artifact-produced) so it can no longer infer "empty run /
  no synthesis" from one blind row (BUG2); rewrite the prompt to require
  evidence-grounding and allow abstention (BUG3).
- gradient_extractor: cap confidence below the 0.6 injection bar for rows with
  no captured evidence (the telemetry gap) so unfounded claims can't be injected
  as lessons (BUG4b / BUG1 mitigation).
- gradient_extractor: absorb near-duplicate gradients without ratcheting their
  confidence upward, so a repeated confabulation can't climb past the bar (BUG5).
- execute: a synthesizer node no longer stamps the confabulated
  reviewer_verdict='unknown' onto its trace (BUG6).
- trace_store: a rubric parse_error is a no-op instead of stamping reward_g=-1
  across every trace of the run (BUG7).

Verified live against a copy of the real feature-inv-20260730-224613 run:
mechanical smoke passes all gates; the codex-lane real dispatch correctly
abstains on a grounded node with no "empty run" confabulation; 184 targeted
unit tests green. Three tests that pinned the old (buggy) contract were
migrated with explanatory comments.
subject: fix(learning): stop the gradient/reward loop confabulating on empty + ungrounded traces

problem_statement:
fix(dispatch): sever controlling terminal + group-kill hung harnesses (SE-3 Phase A.1)

core.dispatch is the sole subprocess spawn seam for every harness lane, so
its process contract is where the SE-3 incident's Layer 1 (a /dev/tty prompt
blocking a headless run) is closed once, structurally — not by every caller
remembering MINI_ORK_NONINTERACTIVE=1.

- start_new_session=True: the child (and everything it spawns) becomes its own
  session with no controlling terminal, so no code path — mini-ork's own
  plan.py prompt or a harness CLI — can open /dev/tty and block a headless run.
- On timeout, os.killpg SIGKILLs the whole detached process *group*, not just
  the direct child. A hung lane can no longer orphan grandchildren (claude's
  helpers, codex's sidecar) that keep burning cost, and freeing the inherited
  stdout pipe those grandchildren hold is what unblocks the drain communicate().
- subprocess.run -> Popen + communicate so we hold the handle needed to reap
  the group; behaviour otherwise preserved (prompt over stdin = E2BIG-proof,
  faithful rc, distinct rc=124 timeout / rc=127 spawn-failure).

tests: +2 process-contract tests (child is a detached session leader with no
reachable /dev/tty; a timeout reaps a grandchild via group-kill). 220 existing
dispatch/core tests green.
subject: fix(dispatch): sever controlling terminal + group-kill hung harnesses (SE-3 Phase A.1)

problem_statement:
fix(plan): gate the /dev/tty prompt on stdin.isatty, not terminal ownership (SE-3 Phase A.1b)

Level-a complement to Phase A.1. A.1 severed the controlling terminal for the
harnesses mini-ork *spawns*; this stops mini-ork *itself* from blocking on a
profile prompt when a parent (the Node BE, a scheduler, CI) hands it an
inherited controlling terminal but no human to answer.

_can_prompt_profile used open('/dev/tty') as its interactivity test — but that
only proves the *session* owns a controlling terminal; it returns True even
when stdin is a pipe or /dev/null. A headless run then took the human-prompt
branch (plan.py:580) and hung forever on input no one would type, instead of
the safe auto-answer path (plan.py:566).

Root fix: gate on the actual presence signal — stdin.isatty() — before touching
/dev/tty. New ordering: explicit MINI_ORK_NONINTERACTIVE opt-out wins, then
stdin must be an interactive tty, then /dev/tty must be reachable. This inverts
the fragile opt-out convention: forgetting the env var now degrades to
auto-answer, never a deadlock. A closed/detached stdin (isatty raises) is
treated as non-interactive rather than letting the exception escape.

tests: +4 guard tests (piped-stdin-with-inherited-tty never prompts;
explicit opt-out beats a real tty; interactive human still prompts; broken
stdin is non-interactive). 73 plan/profile tests green.
subject: fix(plan): gate the /dev/tty prompt on stdin.isatty, not terminal ownership (SE-3 Phase A.1b)

problem_statement:
fix(dispatch): reject wrong-shape lane results at the harness boundary (SE-3 Phase A.2)

Closes the SE-3 incident's Layer 2. A planner lane that returned prose where the
node needs JSON was structurally wrong but ran clean, so dispatch_with_fallback
(which accepts the first `ok and text.strip()` result) served it, attempted no
fallback, wrote the broken text to an out_file, and the run died ~20 min later
when validate_artifact finally tried to parse it. The failure was invisible at
the one seam that could have retried it.

Root fix: an optional *structural* predicate at the dispatch boundary.
- mini_ork/dispatch/predicates.py: `looks_like_json(result)` — "is it even JSON",
  fail-open (True when in doubt so a legit-but-unusual result is never dropped),
  tolerant of ```json fences and prose-wrapped objects. `SHAPE_REJECT_RC = 65`
  (EX_DATAERR) so a shape reject is distinguishable from timeout (124) / spawn
  failure (127). Deliberately NOT a semantic validator — right keys / schema
  stays validate_artifact's job, so a second drifting copy of the schema can't
  grow here.
- dispatch_with_fallback gains `accept: Callable[[DispatchResult], bool] | None`.
  A lane that returns ok+non-empty text but fails `accept` is now a
  fallback-triggering failure. If every lane fails the shape check, the last
  result is returned downgraded to ok=False / rc=65 via dataclasses.replace —
  the caller sees "wrong shape", never a false success.
- Single-lane path (no fallback target) applies the same downgrade in
  mo_llm_dispatch, so the single-lane and multi-lane contracts match.
- A minimal node→shape registry at the llm_dispatch CLI (`{"planner":
  looks_like_json}`, kill switch MO_SHAPE_CHECK=0) gates only nodes whose JSON
  contract is confirmed — prose nodes (researcher/reviewer/reflector) are never
  false-rejected. The registry is NOT derived from artifact_contract.yaml (that
  coupling is the drift this design avoids).
- Threading guard: a caller/test-supplied dispatch_fn keeps its historic 5-arg
  contract; `accept=` is passed only when dispatch_fn is None (the default
  dispatcher). Pinned by test_custom_dispatch_fn_never_receives_accept.

Design fixed by a unanimous 3/3 subagent consensus (Reliability · Builder ·
Future-Maintainer); decision record + evidence index in
internal-docs/research/2026-08-04-harness-engine-standardization.md §10.

tests: +17 (predicate structural cases; fallback on wrong shape; all-lanes
shape-reject; accept=None backward-compat; single-lane downgrade; CLI
accept-threading contract for gated vs prose nodes). dispatch-adjacent suites
green (14 + 23).
subject: fix(dispatch): reject wrong-shape lane results at the harness boundary (SE-3 Phase A.2)

problem_statement:
fix(SE-3): docker env injection via bare -e KEY, off the ps-readable argv

Close the host `ps aux` secret exposure at both docker `-e` sites (spawn +
up). Previously each allowlisted key crossed as `-e KEY=VALUE`, putting API
keys in the docker client's argv for the full lifetime of a run — readable
by any local user. Now forward the key by NAME only (`-e KEY`, no value):
docker reads the value from the client process's own environment, so it
lives only in /proc/<pid>/environ (owner+root), the protection a 0600
--env-file gives with no tempfile to create, chmod, or unlink on crash.

- spawn: emit sorted bare `-e KEY` for the allowlisted keys and launch
  subprocess.run(env={**os.environ, **allowed}); the allowlist still fully
  governs WHAT crosses — this only moves the value off argv.
- up: same bare `-e KEY` for env_passthrough (the `_docker` subprocess
  inherits our env).
- microVM path unchanged: it already passes env as a structured SDK arg
  (sb.exec(env=)), never host argv — no exposure.

Resolves follow-up #2 in the decision doc (was: evaluate --env-file); bare
-e is strictly simpler. Tests: flip the env-shape assertion to the bare-name
form + a regression test that no secret VALUE appears in argv; the live
docker round-trip already proves the value still crosses.

Verified: 33 passed (docker spawn incl. 2 live round-trip/timeout,
workspace_env, isolation selector), ruff --select F,E9 clean, live
`docker exec -e MO_SECRET_PROBE` forwards the value while `ps aux` shows
only the bare name.
subject: fix(SE-3): docker env injection via bare -e KEY, off the ps-readable argv

problem_statement:
fix(self-improve): revert main-checkout leaks so a rejected iteration leaves main pristine

The self-improve loop edits a linked worktree that lives under the main tree
(.mini-ork/worktrees/iter-N-ts). The implementer harness has been observed
writing the patch back into the parent checkout instead of the worktree
(linked-worktree path resolution), so a rejected iteration could leave modified
tracked files and stray untracked files in main — iter-1 leaked verify.py +
test_verify.py that had to be hand-reverted.

Add a surface-scoped leak guard:
- _root_surface_dirty(root): NUL-delimited `git status --porcelain` over the
  improvable surface (mini_ork/ recipes/ schemas/ tests/), returning the set of
  currently-dirty paths.
- _restore_root_surface_leak(root, pre_dirty): reverts only paths that went
  clean->dirty during the run (checkout HEAD for tracked, remove for untracked);
  paths the operator already had dirty pre-run are never touched, so concurrent
  hand-edits are safe.

Snapshot pre_dirty before dispatch; restore after outcome is decided, before
`git worktree remove`, and log restored paths. Promotion still flows only through
the worktree branch + merge, never the main working tree.

test_restore_root_surface_leak: builds a temp repo with an operator WIP file,
simulates a run leaking a tracked mutation + an untracked file + an
outside-surface change; asserts only the two in-surface leaks are reverted and
the WIP + outside-surface change are untouched. self_improve unit 7/7.
subject: fix(self-improve): revert main-checkout leaks so a rejected iteration leaves main pristine

problem_statement:
fix(security): close pty run_id traversal + harden exec allow-list (CodeQL #46-48)

CodeQL flagged the WebSocket PTY bridge on three counts. One is a real bug; two
are the allow-list not being visible to the taint analyzer. Both are addressed
at the sink so the guarantee is explicit for a reader and a scanner alike.

- pty.py:66 (#47, path expression) — REAL. `run_id` arrives off a query param
  and was joined onto `home/runs/` unchecked, so `run_id=../../../../etc` moved
  the orchestrator's cwd anywhere on disk. Add `_is_safe_run_id` (single
  traversal-free segment: no separators, NUL, or parent refs) plus a realpath
  containment check that the resolved dir still lives under `runs/`. A hostile
  value now falls back to the project root instead of escaping it.

- pty.py:127 (#46 command line, #48 path expression) — the harness is already
  allow-listed by `resolve_harness`, but an `x in ALLOWED_HARNESSES` guard
  returns the same tainted object, so CodeQL kept tracing the `cmd` param to
  `execvp`. Route the harness through a `_HARNESS_PROGRAM` dict of string
  literals: looking a validated name up yields a constant, severing the taint
  edge into every exec/subprocess sink (harness_argv, session_name,
  _launch_command). Behavior is byte-identical for the vetted harnesses; an
  unrecognized name falls back to a login shell rather than executing itself.

- tests/unit/test_pty_py.py — pin the traversal guard: real run dir resolves,
  hostile run_ids (.., absolute, embedded sep/NUL) all fall back to the project
  root, and `_is_safe_run_id` accepts plain segments / rejects the rest.
subject: fix(security): close pty run_id traversal + harden exec allow-list (CodeQL #46-48)

problem_statement:
fix(dispatch): resolve lens-lane aliases to family before building the fallback chain

A node pinned to a *_lens lane (e.g. codex_lens) silently dispatched to
minimax instead of its intended family. dispatch_node fed the raw agents.yaml
alias into dispatch_chain as the fallback-chain lead; dispatch preflight keys
on providers.yaml model names, so a *_lens alias fails preflight ("unknown
lane") and the MO_FALLBACK_CODING head (minimax) silently serves.

resolve_lane_family() maps an alias to its lanes.<alias> family model (fail-open
on any error / missing agents.yaml). The chain lead now resolves to the real
family so the alias leads and the MO_FALLBACK_* tail stays a genuine fallback.
lane itself is unchanged — still used verbatim for trace() and capability asserts.

Regression + ratchet in tests/unit/test_lane_chain_resolution.py.
subject: fix(dispatch): resolve lens-lane aliases to family before building the fallback chain

problem_statement:
fix(review): reject list-valued source_artifact in synth artifact naming

A reviewer/synth node resolves its output filename from the recipe's
artifact_contract.yaml `source_artifact`. When that value is a YAML list
(the stale D-037 "input staging" form), `_synth_artifact_name` returned the
list and `os.path.join(run_dir, <list>)` threw an opaque TypeError deep in
posixpath. Because the reviewer node runs in a ProcessPool child, the
traceback never crossed the pool boundary — the crash surfaced only as
"N node(s) failed", undiagnosable from the parent's stderr.

Raise a clear ValueError naming the recipe + key when source_artifact is a
non-string, and capture the child-process traceback in the isolated native
worker so a future in-child failure is diagnosable from the parent.
subject: fix(review): reject list-valued source_artifact in synth artifact naming

problem_statement:
fix(cli): load the secret store into os.environ at main() entry (bash-source parity)

The retired bash dispatcher sourced secrets.local.sh at startup, so
MO_*/MINI_ORK_* overrides in the store reached every child process --
nodes, transports, AND verifiers. Native dispatch fed the store only to
provider_environment(), which silently stranded non-credential overrides
outside verifier subprocess envs: MINI_ORK_TYPECHECK_CMD set in the
store never reached the typecheck verifier, whose auto-detect then
picked a repo guarded always-exit-1 script and false-failed the run
(observed on run-1788338054, skipping reviewer/eval/publisher lanes).

Load with setdefault so real environment variables still win; an
unreadable store degrades to a stderr warning (mirrors the doctor
handler) so mini-ork help never fails on a mis-permissioned file.
subject: fix(cli): load the secret store into os.environ at main() entry (bash-source parity)

problem_statement:
fix(learning): score 'failure' rows via the reward base band, not the unknown-status early return

in the validity-masking suite. Found by the 2026-09-10 opus+minimax audit
panel (F1, both judges confirmed).

problem_statement:
fix(client): pin embedding interpreter for launcher spawns; 6 tests env-proof

Five tests (launcher x3, resume no-sentinel, SDK dry-run) exec bin/mini-ork
bare and inherit the shebang's /usr/bin/env python3 — on machines whose PATH
python3 is a bare pyenv python without mini-ork's deps, every invocation
dies at `import yaml` before any CLI logic runs (red suite on the dev box,
green in CI, green on fresh worktrees: pure interpreter luck).

The SDK fix is the real one: MiniOrk is an EMBEDDING facade — the importing
process already runs an interpreter under which mini_ork's deps are
importable, so _cli_command pins sys.executable ahead of the launcher path
for run/init/classify/spawn. The shebang stays a human-shell convenience and
stays statically asserted. Test invokers (launcher goldens, resume closure)
pin the same way.

Sixth: test_empty_cwd_inherits compared path SPELLINGS; behind this host's
firmlink (/Volumes/docker-ssd ≡ /Users/admin) the child bash prints the
physical spelling while pytest keeps the logical one. Compare resolved
paths — the inherit contract is about the directory, not its spelling.

Full suite: 2880 passed, 0 failed.
subject: fix(client): pin embedding interpreter for launcher spawns; 6 tests env-proof

problem_statement:
fix(code-fix): publish reviewer verdict; split eval onto judge lane (#201)

* fix(code-fix): publish reviewer verdict; split eval onto judge lane

Two independent defects kept the code-fix recipe from routing to a
heterogeneous fleet and from ever committing its result.

1. The publisher node could never commit. `_publisher_try_commit_files`
   reads `REVIEW_FILE` and `VERDICT` from the environment, but nothing in
   the Python engine ever published them — a leftover from the bash
   `_dispatch_node`, which used to export them. Its only other verdict
   candidates (`panel-verdict.json`, `review-verdict.json`) are panel-gate
   artifacts that recipes like code-fix never write, so the resolved
   verdict was unconditionally `'<none>'` and every run logged
   `[skip-publish] ... is not APPROVE — no commit`. `_handle_reviewer` now
   publishes both after extracting the verdict.

   Reproduced and verified against the real `_publisher_try_commit_files`
   in a scratch repo: pre-fix shape → `committed = False`; post-fix shape
   → `committed = True` with the `mini-ork(code-fix): ...` commit.

2. The `eval` node could not run on its intended judge lane. Its
   `model_lane` was `reviewer`, and the node's *resolved* lane is what gets
   published into `MO_DISPATCH_CHAIN` — which `_default_llm_dispatch`
   reads before the jury's per-juror lane argument. So the judge was
   pinned to Opus and `MO_EVAL_JURY_LANES` was inert. The node now has a
   dedicated `judge` lane, mapped in `config/agents.yaml`.

No behaviour change for recipes that do not use a classic reviewer or an
eval node.

* fix(execute): make the code-fix publisher commit path reachable

The publisher's commit gate reads two run-dir artifacts, and nothing in the
code-fix recipe ever wrote either one — so a run that passed typecheck, tests,
and review still could not commit:

1. review-verdict.json — the reviewer's verdict was handed over via publish_env.
   Nodes execute in a ProcessPoolExecutor (cli/execute.py), so that write dies
   with the reviewer's worker process and the publisher's own process observes
   nothing; REVIEW_FILE/VERDICT read as "". Write the verdict to run_dir instead
   (publisher._publisher_try_commit_files already scans for it there).

2. implementer-summary.json — only the self-migrate path wrote one, and
   _write_self_migrate_implementer_summary has zero callers. Add
   _write_implementer_summary and call it from _handle_implementer. It derives
   files_changed from the working tree rather than the model's self-report,
   scoped by <run_dir>/pre-implementer-ref so a concurrent session's pre-existing
   dirt is never swept into the commit.

Also report the actual non-approving verdict in the skip message: '<none>' when
a reviewer returned verdict='fail' reads as "no verdict found at all" and sends
the reader hunting a file that is present.

Tests cover both writers and the full implementer → reviewer → publisher seam
with review_file="" and verdict_env="" (the production condition under the
process split).
subject: fix(code-fix): publish reviewer verdict; split eval onto judge lane (#201)

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): wire sweep implementer node + per-unit kickoff templating

The sweep submode was registered under node_id=sweep_dispatcher, a
transform node — implementer submodes are only consulted in
_handle_implementer, so sweep_run() never fired and waves planned
children without spawning them (driver killed the loop as
diverged:no_progress). Add a real `sweep` implementer node between
sweep_dispatcher and goal_check and re-key the submode.

_default_spawn_fn now materializes {{unit_id}}/{{reason}} into the
child kickoff per unit (filesystem-safe slug filenames — unit ids are
usually relative paths containing '/'); static file templates without
placeholders pass through unchanged. Submode scripts run on
sys.executable instead of ambient python3 so `import mini_ork` keeps
resolving inside the venv.
subject: fix(goal-loop): wire sweep implementer node + per-unit kickoff templating

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): let the wave's own kickoff differ from the child kickoff

_default_run_wave_fn shelled `mini-ork run goal-loop <kickoff>` using
MO_GOAL_CHILD_KICKOFF — the per-unit fix template that _default_spawn_fn
templates {{unit_id}}/{{reason}} into. Feeding the child's editorial
"edit this ONE file" template to the wave's own goal-loop run is a
category error. Prefer a dedicated MO_GOAL_WAVE_KICKOFF, falling back to
MO_GOAL_CHILD_KICKOFF for zero regression.
subject: fix(goal-loop): let the wave's own kickoff differ from the child kickoff

problem_statement:
fix(rsi): make rollback a real backstop, and stop documenting gates that are not there

The human approval gate is gone (0a9afc3a), so rollback is what stands behind an
unattended promote. It could not restore anything: `rollback()` raised for every
live row. Four independent causes, each fixed:

  1. `register()` never wrote `promoted_at`, so the `ORDER BY promoted_at DESC`
     lookups in `current()` / `rollback()` were non-deterministic.
  2. The first promotion of a name had no predecessor row, so
     `previous_stable_version` was NULL and there was nowhere to roll back to.
     `register()` now mints a baseline row carrying `baseline_content` when the
     caller supplies it, stamped one second earlier so the order is total.
  3. The payload stored a `rollback_hash`, not text, so even with a predecessor
     the DB could not restore bytes. Both texts are now stored.
  4. `rollback()` only moved status columns. It now writes the content back to
     `target_path` — the status update alone leaves the retired directive on
     disk, so the system that "rolled back" keeps executing what it retired.

The file write refuses to run when `target_path` sits outside `MINI_ORK_ROOT`,
and says so: a long-lived DB accumulates absolute paths into whichever worktree
promoted them, and restoring one would silently rewrite a different checkout. A
failed write raises rather than being swallowed, and every restore announces
itself on stderr so "reverted" can be read as "bytes restored".

`_handle_rollback` also rolled back `("agent", "default")`. No row is named
that — an applied prompt mutation is named by its absolute target path — so the
agent half was a guaranteed no-op that still reported success. It now resolves
the run's applied targets from the implementer's recorded `files_changed` via
`version_registry.targets_for_paths`. The sidecar copy is dropped in favour of
the in-DB content.

Docs corrected against the code, because they were the safety posture's only
advertisement and three claims were false:

  * `mini-ork version-clear-quarantine` does not exist. `promote.py` advertised
    it too; clearing a quarantine is a Python-level call, and it is a stronger
    block than the docs implied — `_previously_failed` stops a quarantined
    directive from being re-proposed at all.
  * Nothing writes `audit_log`. The table and its append-only triggers exist
    (0012_safety.sql); the machine-readable trail is `version_registry` +
    `apply_attempts` + `promotion_records`.
  * There is no `config/safety.yaml`, no `workflow_versions` table, and the
    `safety_constraints` table has no writer — so no declarative constraints
    file backstops the loop. What does is the measurement gate plus your VCS,
    which is what the README now says.

README states plainly that this is recursive self-improvement, that the human
gate was removed deliberately, and that no flag restores it.

Tests: 2639 passed, 13 skipped. The legacy pre-content rollback path is pinned
by its own test rather than tolerated as stderr noise.
subject: fix(rsi): make rollback a real backstop, and stop documenting gates that are not there

problem_statement:
fix(publisher): keep bare-relative outputs run-local, not repo-root commits

A bare relative artifact_contract output (no directory component) -- e.g.
goal-loop's panel-verdict.json -- was joined against the mini-ork repo root
and then git-committed there, landing a stray "audit(<recipe>): publish
synthesis from <run>" commit on the repo root on every wave. The run_local
guard could never catch it: dst was already resolved against root, so a bare
name never satisfied the run_root prefix test.

Resolve a bare-name output against run_dir (its canonical producer-written
location) so it is preserved in place -- never copied or committed to root.
Relative paths WITH a directory component (docs/refactor/foo.md) stay
repo-relative publish targets; absolute ${MINI_ORK_RUN_DIR}/foo paths are
unchanged. Same latent leak is fixed for blog-cohesion, book-gen-flow-audit,
and chapter-review bare-name outputs.

Regression test asserts the verdict never lands at the repo root and HEAD does
not advance; verified to fail on the pre-fix publisher.
subject: fix(publisher): keep bare-relative outputs run-local, not repo-root commits

problem_statement:
fix(reflect): emergent-pattern gate counts independent runs, not list length

The automatic reflect path approved a pattern at strength >= 3 with
n_evidence >= 1, where n_evidence was len(json.loads(member_item_ids_json))
— a raw list length with no distinctness check. One trace id repeated three
times cleared the floor, and so did three traces from a single run. Only
'approved' rows reach the agent's context, so this was the poisoning-to-
influence path, and it fires unattended at run end.

Evidence is now measured as DISTINCT runs behind the named trace ids:
  * a repeated trace id is one observation;
  * N traces sharing one run_id are one observation;
  * a NULL/empty run_id is unproven independence and counts zero;
  * an unresolvable trace id counts zero.
A missing traces table falls back to the distinct-id count rather than
crashing reflection.

MO_EMERGENT_VERIFY_MIN_EVIDENCE now clamps UP only (max(3, env)): a safety
floor is not a setting, and no env var may restore the forgeable bar.

Verified live through `mini-ork reflect`: a pattern backed by one trace id
repeated three times and one backed by three traces from one run both stay
'proposed'; a pattern backed by three traces across three distinct runs is
approved.

Tests updated deliberately, not weakened: the gate test now seeds real
traces with distinct run_ids, and five cases pin the independence rule
(repeated id, one run, NULL run_id, floor cannot be lowered, floor can be
raised).
subject: fix(reflect): emergent-pattern gate counts independent runs, not list length

problem_statement:
fix(promote): require independent benchmark runs, not sample count

promotion_evaluate aggregated every benchmark_results row for a candidate
and never read run_id. One run emitting 30 passing rows was therefore
indistinguishable from 30 runs agreeing, so a single benchmark execution
could promote a candidate on 30 samples of one observation. Both the
samples and the all_pass flag came from the same run.

Independence is now measured separately from the sample count:
`_evidence_run_ids` returns the distinct run_id values behind a candidate,
and the decision tree rejects when that count is below
max(3, MO_PROMOTION_MIN_RUNS). The env var may raise the floor but never
lower it — a floor an environment can lower is not a floor.

A NULL/blank run_id is unproven independence and counts zero, and nothing
backfills a synthetic id: that would fabricate the exact independence being
demanded. The migrated schema declares run_id INTEGER NOT NULL so this
cannot arise there, but the guard holds for loose and legacy tables.

promotion_records.benchmark_run_id now records which runs the decision
rested on instead of a bare NULL, so the audit trail can answer the one
question a promotion has to answer. A multi-run decision has no single
benchmark_memory.summary_id to name, so the column carries the
comma-joined run list; application connections never enable FK
enforcement, and a promote resting on several runs is exactly the case the
column previously could not express.

Verified live through `mini-ork promote`: 30 passing rows all from run 1
give decision=rejected, rationale "insufficient independent evidence: 1
distinct run(s), 3 required; 30 sample(s) recorded", candidate left in
shadow with no version bump; the same 30 rows spread across runs 1-3
promote with n_runs=3.

Tests updated deliberately, not weakened: the all-pass seed helper now
spreads its rows across 3 distinct runs (four samples from one run can no
longer clear the floor however well they pass), and four new cases pin the
independence rule (single run rejected, floor cannot be lowered, floor can
be raised, NULL/blank run_id dropped).
subject: fix(promote): require independent benchmark runs, not sample count

problem_statement:
fix(promote): authority-capture check fails CLOSED when it cannot run

`_cw_por_compute` answered 'default_passed' when the checker could not be
imported and 'indeterminate_default_passed' when it raised, and the caller
in `mo_promote_synthesis_gate` blocked only on 'failed'. All three statuses
therefore cleared the CW-POR condition and fell through to the structural
check — so deleting the checker, breaking its import, or feeding it a panel
with no ground truth silently *permitted* the promote instead of catching
authority capture. The check that exists to stop a captured panel from
licensing itself was itself a way to license a promote.

The statuses are now named for what happened and only an affirmative
'passed' clears the condition:

  * 'unavailable'   — import failed; no check happened.
  * 'error'         — the checker raised.
  * 'indeterminate' — it ran but found no ground-truth signal to compute from.
  * 'failed'        — authority capture suspected (unchanged).
  * 'passed'        — panel healthy (unchanged).

The caller's comparison is widened from `cw_status == "failed"` to
`cw_status != "passed"`, with 'failed' keeping its own `authority_capture`
reason code so the pre-existing blocking path is unchanged. Everything else
rejects as `cw_por_unverified`. A panel with no ground truth is *unmeasured*
capture, not absent capture, and the difference now decides the outcome.

This closes the last fail-open in the promotion path and completes the set
begun by B1 and B2: an unavailable or forgeable check must not resolve to
permission.

test_mo_promote_synthesis_gate_rejections case (b) is updated deliberately,
not weakened: it seeded an empty `voters` list, which is now rejected earlier
as cw_por_unverified, so it could no longer prove the structural condition is
reachable. It now seeds a correctly-labelled panel that clears CW-POR, which
tests the same thing more precisely.

New test_cw_por_fail_closed.py pins all three fail-closed statuses, the two
statuses that must still work, and asserts the retired fail-open names are
not produced by the function body — so the escape hatch cannot return by
rename. Its import-blocking helper drops the cached parent-package attribute
as well as blanking sys.modules, because `from X import Y` reaches the
attribute first and a sys.modules-only monkeypatch would pass when it ran
first and silently fail to block when it ran third.

Verified live: a verdict clearing panel_score and all three structural
signals gives decision=approved when the checker is present, and
decision=rejected / reason=cw_por_unverified (rc=1) once the checker module
is removed.
subject: fix(promote): authority-capture check fails CLOSED when it cannot run

problem_statement:
fix(env): the run contract must survive the transport's second filter

Found by the S1 live-container probe, not by the unit tests.

S1 routes the recursive child through the Workspace axis: `cli/spawn.py` filters
the AMBIENT host env through `container_env`, then injects the child's identity
on top. But a backend's `spawn` filters the env it is handed a SECOND time — and
`MINI_ORK_*` matches neither the `MO_*` prefix nor the `*_API_KEY` suffix, so that
second pass stripped all five keys and the child launched anonymous.

Proved live under MO_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker with a probe CLI on the drive: the
child saw ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (allowlisted, correctly crossed), no host secret and
the container's own PATH (correctly excluded) — and every one of MINI_ORK_HOME /
_DB / _RUN_ID / _PARENT_RUN_ID / _ALLOW_CHILD_SPAWN as `<unset>`. A real mini-ork
child in that state resolves a fresh MINI_ORK_HOME off its cwd and loses the whole
run lineage. The same re-filter is on the shipped SE-3 dispatch path
(`_spawn_in_workspace` hands the backend proc_env), so this was a pre-existing
hole that S1 made load-bearing.

`_RUN_CONTRACT_KEYS` re-admits exactly those five key NAMES, which makes filtering
an already-assembled env idempotent. Deliberately an exact-name set and NOT a
`MINI_ORK_` prefix: the namespace stays closed, so MINI_ORK_ROOT / a host
MINI_ORK_HOME / MINI_ORK_SECRETS still cannot ride, and a forgotten override keeps
failing LOUD in the child rather than silently pointing it at a host path that
does not exist inside the sandbox.

One place covers both backends — docker and microvm import the SAME policy object
(asserted by test_both_backends_share_one_policy_object).

Verified: tests/unit/test_workspace_env.py + test_docker_spawn.py +
test_microvm_spawn.py + test_spawn_workspace_isolation_py.py → 50 passed,
3 skipped. Live re-probe on docker: all five contract keys now arrive with the
CONTAINER view (MINI_ORK_HOME=/workspace, RUN_ID=c-env), MINI_ORK_ROOT still
absent, host secret still absent, rc=0, no leftover containers.
subject: fix(env): the run contract must survive the transport's second filter

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): keep the worktree edit on rollback when an outer loop owns verify

In the RSI goal-loop the code-fix child's in-sandbox glm reviewer is both
redundant and evidence-starved: the run's verifiers are scoped to echo-stubs
(to dodge the 17k-file researcher build) and the diff capture comes back empty,
so the reviewer returns needs_revision on a fix that is actually correct. That
escalates_to the rollback node, whose revert_branch strategy then REVERTS the
implementer's verified edit out of the worktree -- before goal_apply can deploy
it. The deploy therefore runs a fix-less worktree, the chapter re-fails, and the
wave burns a 90-min regen await for nothing.

The authoritative verifier in a closed RSI loop is downstream: deploy -> regen
-> DB flip (committed_complete + rubric_status=pass), not the in-sandbox
reviewer. Add MINI_ORK_ROLLBACK_KEEP_WORKTREE: when set, _handle_rollback still
runs the version-registry/DB rollback but SKIPS _revert_working_tree, preserving
FILE state so the outer loop can test the real edit. The shared code-fix recipe
keeps its safe default (revert on reject) for standalone runs; only the
goal-loop driver opts in.

launch-armed.sh exports the flag (default 1) so the spawned code-fix child
inherits it via spawn.py's {**os.environ, **overrides} local-transport env.
subject: fix(goal-loop): keep the worktree edit on rollback when an outer loop owns verify

problem_statement:
fix(sandbox): carry MINI_ORK_ROLLBACK_KEEP_WORKTREE across the transport boundary

fb37622e added the rollback keep-worktree lever and verified it through the
local transport, where the child env is built as {**os.environ, **overrides}
and nothing re-filters. On the sandboxed path (MO_SANDBOX_BACKEND=docker or
microvm) the env is filtered TWICE: once in cli/spawn.py over the ambient env,
then again inside the backend spawn. The second pass admits only
_AGENT_ENV_PREFIXES / *_API_KEY / _RUN_CONTRACT_KEYS, and the new key matched
none of the three, so a sandboxed code-fix child silently fell back to the
default and reverted the very edit the outer goal-loop owns deploying.

Join the key to _RUN_CONTRACT_KEYS, alongside MINI_ORK_ALLOW_CHILD_SPAWN: both
are caller-set policy about the child, not ambient host state, and both are
worthless if stripped at the boundary. The namespace stays closed: MINI_ORK_ROOT
and MINI_ORK_SECRETS (host paths) still drop, asserted.

Tests pin the idempotence that makes the double filter safe, and the negative
case so joining the set cannot quietly open the prefix.
subject: fix(sandbox): carry MINI_ORK_ROLLBACK_KEEP_WORKTREE across the transport boundary

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): fail-fast terminal-failure detection in the apply await

The apply await only stopped on SUCCESS: it polled the pass-predicate until
exit 0 and otherwise burned the entire MO_GOAL_APPLY_AWAIT_SECONDS window
(5400s / 90min live) even when the redispatched regen had already terminally
failed. One bad deploy therefore cost 90 min before the outer driver could
quarantine / re-plan.

Add an optional, opt-in failure probe alongside the success probe:

- _poll_until_settled(success_fn, fail_fn, ...) checks success FIRST each cycle
  (a unit that both passed and racily trips the fail probe is reported passed),
  then the fail probe; returns settled/terminal/reason so the consumer can tell
  goal_met from terminal_failure from timeout. fail_fn=None collapses to the
  historical wait-for-success-only loop, so unarmed loops are unchanged.
- _await_terminal builds the pass argv from MO_GOAL_TERMINAL_CMD/PREDICATE_CMD
  and an optional fail argv from MO_GOAL_TERMINAL_FAIL_CMD (unit id always the
  final discrete argv slot, never shell-interpolated).

chapter_terminal_fail.py is the book-goal-loop binding: exit 0 == terminally
failed. permanently_failed=t always fires; status in the failed set is opt-in
(MO_GOAL_FAIL_ON_STATUS_FAILED=1) since a chapter can sit in 'failed'
transiently before a retry; and a STALL (status=generating + fresh last_error +
newest run-* dir under MO_GOAL_RUNS_DIR idle >= MO_GOAL_STALL_SECONDS) is opt-in
too. Run-dir freshness is the stall signal because lifecycle.updated_at stays
frozen at the last chapter milestone during a HEALTHY long generation, so keying
a stall on updated_at would kill healthy long gens. DB error / missing row /
committed_complete stay conservative (non-terminal).

launch-armed.sh wires MO_GOAL_TERMINAL_FAIL_CMD + MO_GOAL_RUNS_DIR +
MO_GOAL_STALL_SECONDS=1200 (20min, ~10x node cadence).

Tests: three run_apply paths (terminal_failure fast / backward-compat timeout /
pass-beats-fail) + hermetic binding guards and the run-dir freshness helper.
subject: fix(goal-loop): fail-fast terminal-failure detection in the apply await

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): fail-fast on worker-exhausted-idle, not just generating-stall

The #36 terminal-failure detector only tripped on status=generating with an
idle run-dir (orphaned mid-generation). Live monitoring of book d0df3cdb showed
the DOMINANT stall is different: the worker burns its per-dispatch retry budget
(generation_attempts climbs to 6 = two cycles of 3), leaves the chapter failed
(NOT permanently_failed), and goes idle. The old detector missed this, so
drive.py await sat out the full 90-min MO_GOAL_APPLY_AWAIT_SECONDS window on a
chapter only a redispatch could advance.

Broaden the stall set to _STALL_STATUSES = {generating, failed, error} and keep
the idle-run-dir gate as the safe discriminator: a chapter racily failed BETWEEN
retries still has a churning worker (fresh run-*), so age < stall => NOT
terminal; only a genuinely stopped worker (age >= stall) trips it. This is
strictly safer than MO_GOAL_FAIL_ON_STATUS_FAILED, which fires on failed
immediately and would abandon a chapter mid-retry.

3 new hermetic tests mock the psql wrapper _q and stamp run-dir mtimes:
worker-exhausted-idle=terminal, failed-but-churning=not-terminal,
permfail=always-terminal. 33 pass.
subject: fix(goal-loop): fail-fast on worker-exhausted-idle, not just generating-stall

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): per-unit fingerprint divergence + patience windows

The armed book campaign (driver 13102) exited rc=0 at WAVE 2 with
stop=diverged (no_progress) despite --max-waves 24, while 9 of 10 chapters
sat untouched. Root cause: the divergence signature keyed on the full
failing-unit SET, but MAX_CHILDREN_PER_WAVE=1 attempts exactly one chapter
per wave against 10 units — the set cannot shrink until a whole chapter
lands, so an unchanged set is guaranteed every wave and no_progress fired at
the earliest possible moment. GRAO quarantine was degenerate the same way:
fix_hash keyed on unit_id only, so every surviving unit accrued two identical
hashes by wave 2 and would have tripped all_quarantined next.

Both detectors now read real per-unit progress, using data the wave already
produces:

- wave_signature folds each unit's failure FINGERPRINT (status + failing
  node, parsed from goal-state.json, volatile attempts/mdlen counters
  stripped) so a fix that MOVES a chapter's failure W9->W15 or clears it
  counts as progress even before the failing set shrinks. reasons=None
  reproduces the historical set-only signature byte-for-byte.
- quarantine hashes are scoped to the units a wave ACTUALLY attempted
  (sweep-result.json), so a pending chapter the single-child loop never
  reached does not accrue identical hashes and cannot spuriously trip
  all_quarantined.
- divergence() and the quarantine threshold take a patience window
  (MO_GOAL_DIVERGENCE_PATIENCE / MO_GOAL_QUARANTINE_PATIENCE, default 2 to
  preserve the all-units-per-wave contract; the book launcher sets 6) so the
  code-fix child gets several waves to land a real researcher fix before the
  loop declares a unit hopeless.

_default_run_wave_fn threads unit_reasons + attempted from goal-state.json
and sweep-result.json into the wave verdict. 8 new hermetic tests: fingerprint
strips counters / keeps node, moved-failure changes the signature, patience
window, attempted-scoped hashing, book loop survives to wave 4 and lands,
book loop still diverges when truly stuck (at the window, not before), pending
units never trip all_quarantined. 30 driver + 33 recipe tests pass.
subject: fix(goal-loop): per-unit fingerprint divergence + patience windows

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): quarantine-aware wave selection rotates off stuck units

The armed book campaign could only ever work chapter 1. goal_sweep_plan
selected failing units by string-sorting them and taking the first
MAX_CHILDREN_PER_WAVE, and the book launcher runs one child per wave over
10 chapters. string-sort puts "1" first, so the single child slot went to
unit "1" every single wave; chapters 2-10 (which the live DB shows sitting
at status=pending, attempts=0, with 12-46k of draft content and NO worker
touching them) were never selected. Even with the wave-2 divergence fix
letting the loop run all 24 waves, all 24 would re-hammer the one broken
chapter and the other nine would never converge.

The driver already computes a GRAO quarantine set (a unit stuck for the
whole patience window) but never fed it back into selection — quarantine
was report-only. Now it steers the hunt:

- _default_run_wave_fn exports the quarantine set as MO_GOAL_QUARANTINED_UNITS
  (newline-sorted) into the wave recipe subprocess.
- goal_sweep_plan's new pure core _select_units EXCLUDES those units before
  capping, so once chapter 1 is quarantined the freed child slot rotates onto
  chapter 2, then 3, ... — the loop finally reaches every failing chapter.
- selection is numeric-aware (_unit_sort_key) so rotation follows natural
  ch1->ch2->ch3 order instead of string order (1,10,2,3,...).
- starvation guard: if EVERY failing unit is quarantined the exclusion is
  dropped so the wave still dispatches and the driver's all_quarantined stop
  ends the loop cleanly, rather than the selector silently emitting an empty
  plan.

Backward-compatible: MO_GOAL_QUARANTINED_UNITS unset/blank reproduces the
historical selection byte-for-byte, so a running campaign that picks up the
new transforms.py mid-flight (its old driver never sets the env) is a no-op.

5 new hermetic tests: numeric-before-string ordering, first-failing pick in
natural order, quarantine exclusion rotates the slot, starvation guard keeps
dispatching, passing units skipped; plus the driver exports the sorted set
into the recipe env. 69 goal-loop tests pass, ruff F/E9 clean.
subject: fix(goal-loop): quarantine-aware wave selection rotates off stuck units

problem_statement:
fix(recipe-resolution): honor MINI_ORK_HOME overlay so verified-artifact resolves

The env-shadow bug that reds W9: mini-ork resolved recipes only from
MINI_ORK_ROOT/recipes, but a consumer (the researcher) symlinks its private
verified-artifact overlay into MINI_ORK_HOME/recipes while the spawn still
leaks MINI_ORK_ROOT=primary. The two disagreed -> "no recipe: verified-artifact"
(exit_code=2) even though the overlay was present.

main._resolve_recipe_base now prefers MINI_ORK_HOME/recipes/<recipe> when that
dir exists, else falls back to root (byte-for-byte historical for dev checkouts
whose home has no recipes/). The winning base is threaded via a new
MINI_ORK_RECIPE_ROOT env var; execute.py and execute_handlers.py grow a local
_recipe_root() so every recipe-asset join (register.py, workflow.yaml,
artifact_contract.yaml, prompts, verifiers, implementer submode script) follows
the recipe to where it was actually found instead of re-resolving from primary.

gen_profile reads task_class.yaml + artifact_contract.yaml from the resolved
base. +7 unit tests cover the overlay-wins / root-fallback / _->- swap /
not-found / home==root-dedup paths and an end-to-end W9 regression asserting
MINI_ORK_RECIPE_ROOT + MINI_ORK_WORKFLOW point at the home overlay.

Live-verified: with the exact researcher spawn env, `run verified-artifact`
now resolves (task_class=verified_artifact, 4 nodes) with old-error-count 0.
subject: fix(recipe-resolution): honor MINI_ORK_HOME overlay so verified-artifact resolves

problem_statement:
fix(recursive): per-run child cap counts only non-terminal children

The goal-loop RSI wedged itself. mo_recursive_approve_spawn counted ALL
children ever (COUNT(*) run_spawns WHERE parent_run_id) against
max_children_per_run=4, so a long-lived convergence driver -- one code-fix
child per wave -- permanently blocked further repair waves once 4 children
had accumulated, even though every one of them was TERMINAL (status=failed)
and had already deployed its edit. In-vivo proof: parent
goalloop-armed-20260919-094938 had 4 failed code-fix children that
converted W9 exit_code=2 (contract reject) -> exit_code=1 (critique verdict);
the fingerprint layer saw the progress and wanted a 5th child, but the
lifetime cap vetoed it -> "spawn blocked: parent has 4 children" forever.

The per-run cap is meant to bound OUTSTANDING work, not history. Now it
counts only non-terminal children (excludes completed/failed/merged/rejected),
mirroring max_parallel_children's running-only semantics. Spent children
release their slot; max_total_descendants=16 stays the lifetime runaway
ceiling and the Layer-1 fingerprint/patience quarantine still stops genuinely
stuck units. Each wave is a fresh `mini-ork run goal-loop` subprocess, so the
live driver picks this up on its next wave with no restart.

Tests: terminal children release the budget (3rd spawn succeeds at cap=2);
non-terminal children still block (anti-runaway preserved). 13 passed.
subject: fix(recursive): per-run child cap counts only non-terminal children

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): record real per-wave cost + classify hard-crash failures

The autoraise stop-gate counts only FUNDED waves (cost_usd >= $1), but
_default_run_wave_fn never set cost_usd -- it folded in panel-verdict.json (the
panel node's ~$0 cost), so every wave logged $0 and the predictor's
len(funded) < patience guard stayed true forever: the rail kept rising and the
loop never stopped on funded-but-flat progress. Measure real spend as the
today_cost_usd() delta across the wave subprocess (clamped >= 0 so a starved
wave or 24h-window slide reads 'not funded', never negative).

Make the fix-child kickoff failure-shape-adaptive: ch1's W9_scaffold_sections
now hard-fails (verified-artifact exit_code=1), a different shape than the
heading-drift the kickoff was written around and would mis-steer. Add a
classify-first step + the crash shape pointing the child at the real throw
chain (verifiedArtifactClient.ts -> verifiedArtifact{Production,DagRuntime}.ts,
both touched by the last compose commit) and telling it to reproduce for the
real stderr, since the DB last_error is truncated to ~220 chars.

Regression tests: funded delta recorded over panel's $0; non-positive clamp.
subject: fix(goal-loop): record real per-wave cost + classify hard-crash failures

problem_statement:
fix(reviewer): relativize declared paths so the diff is never silently empty

The reviewer read a 0-byte review-diff.patch and passed a run whose edit it
never saw. Three defects combined to produce that:

1. files_changed is recorded ABSOLUTE (publisher's commit gate and
   _revert_branch both need that shape), but git accepts a pathspec only
   relative to the repo root. An absolute path matched NOTHING and exited 0,
   so the diff was empty and the reviewer was handed "(no diff)".
2. An untracked symlink (baml_client -> a neighbouring checkout) resolved
   outside the worktree via realpath, recording a path that can never be a
   pathspec at all.
3. Nothing distinguished "the implementer changed nothing" from "the capture
   failed", so both read as a clean pass.

_review_pathspecs relativizes the declared entries, drops any that resolve
outside the repo, and drops pathspec magic. _assemble_reviewer_inputs now
widens rather than narrows: when no pathspec survives it captures the whole
delta, since a wider diff can never hide a real edit. When the declared files
are demonstrably unchanged in both the tracked diff and the untracked list,
review-diff-noop.json is written and _handle_reviewer blocks with rc 1 before
any model spend. An untracked new file is real work and is explicitly not a
no-op.

The sweep entry also carried no child_run_id, so the outer loop could not
attribute a wave's outcome to the child that produced it. SpawnResult now
exposes child_run_id/child_run_dir and the driver records child_verdict,
child_failed_nodes, review_diff_bytes and child_no_op alongside it.

Carry-forward: the verifier short-circuit fix (a declared verifier_ref must
run even when artifact_contract.outputs is empty) was sitting uncommitted in
the main checkout; it is included here so the fix is not lost.
subject: fix(reviewer): relativize declared paths so the diff is never silently empty

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): stop this run's env leaking into the deployed worker

The book-goal loop deploys the researcher worker with its own environment, and
that environment carries the goal-loop run's identity. The worker is long-lived
and re-mints a recipe per chapter, so inheriting any of it is wrong.

The live failure: MINI_ORK_PROJECT_HOME outranks MINI_ORK_HOME_DIR in
bin/mini-ork's launcher, so each per-chapter child wrote runs/<id>/
verified-artifact.json into the GOAL-LOOP's .mini-ork while verifiedArtifactClient
read the worktree's — ENOENT, "verifier did not run", for a run that verified
cleanly. Observed on W9_scaffold_sections: 7 attempts, mdlen=0, while chapters
2-10 held tens of KB of uncommitted markdown.

Scrub the run-scoped identity at the spawn source: the recipe/workflow/plan/
profile/node-input pins, the gate commands (pinned to `echo` upstream —
inheriting those would neuter every gate a child runs), the dispatch-chain lane
pin the dispatcher reads straight through as --model, and the home pair. Home
now travels with the replacement pin or not at all: all three home names are
re-pinned to the one resolved home, so no foreign value survives to split the
run dir from its reader.

Deliberately kept: ENGINE_ROOT/ROOT, so children run this loop's engine (main,
with the reviewer-diff and verifier-short-circuit fixes) rather than the
researcher home's older vendored copy; and DB, so the cost circuit keeps
reading the spend it caused.
subject: fix(goal-loop): stop this run's env leaking into the deployed worker

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): close three integrity holes between the fix child and its own grade

The loop's anti-Goodhart backbone (independent re-evaluation via goal_check, a
predicate that lives outside the child's repo, a byte-exact rubric heal) is
sound, but three holes let a child's edit outrun the check that scores it:

A. Instrument guard (transforms.py). committed_complete/rubric_status are
   columns written by researcher code inside the child's own editable tree, and
   scope_gate is a task_class allowlist, not a path filter -- so a child that
   cannot make a chapter pass could instead make PASS MEAN cheaper, and the
   deploy stage would ship it. The guard asks git, per operator-declared glob
   (MO_GOAL_PROTECTED_PATHS), whether the worktree differs from HEAD at any of
   them; if so the deploy REFUSES (fail-closed, including when the git probe
   itself errors) and the wave report names the paths. Generation stays fixable
   -- the DAG runtime the real fix touches is deliberately not listed; only the
   scoring decision is frozen. MO_GOAL_PROTECTED_MODE=warn records without
   refusing; unset globs make the guard completely inert.

B. Objective quality anchor (chapter_quality.py + the predicate hook). Both
   halves of the bar are the researcher's own self-report -- committed_complete
   its "I finished" flag, rubric_status its own G-Eval judge -- so "highest
   quality" rested only on a label the judged code writes. The anchor is a
   deterministic vacuity floor over the bytes the commit path actually persisted
   (no sections / too few / too short / unhashed / mixed doc_version / duplicate
   H2 / unresolved placeholders), living in mini-ork's binding dir so the child
   cannot reach it. Consulted only once the self-report says PASS; enforce by
   default, MO_GOAL_QUALITY_MODE=warn to record only.

C. Real scoped gates (scoped_gate.py). The child's typecheck/test env vars were
   echo stubs, making both mechanical gates pass by construction and leaving the
   LLM reviewer as the only in-sandbox check. Pointing them at the project's
   whole tree is the opposite failure (~17k files, pre-existing diagnostics ->
   phantom-red every wave). scoped_gate takes the middle path: typecheck the
   changed files through a tsconfig that extends the matching project config
   (aliases/strictness intact, scope narrowed via the files array), and run jest
   --findRelatedTests over them. A jest-guard load refusal (rc=77) is a skip,
   not a red.

Tests: 9 guard + 9 quality-anchor cases (incl. a no-false-trip calibration
against the known-good ch1 shape); 106 passed in the goal-loop suite.
subject: fix(goal-loop): close three integrity holes between the fix child and its own grade

problem_statement:
fix(profile): derive target_repo from MO_TARGET_CWD, not the spawn scratch cwd

A spawned child runs with cwd = an empty runs/.../children/<id>/worktree
scratch dir, while MO_TARGET_CWD carries the real target repo. gen_profile
wrote target_repo = Path.cwd(), so every goal-loop child read
target_repo=<empty scratch>, reported 'no source visibility', and no-op'd —
a 0-byte diff the outer loop could never move. Honor the same lever
_resolve_target_cwd already pins for the edit surface.
subject: fix(profile): derive target_repo from MO_TARGET_CWD, not the spawn scratch cwd

problem_statement:
fix(publisher): resolve artifact_contract via MINI_ORK_RECIPE_ROOT, not the engine root

The publisher node joined `root` (the engine checkout) directly when reading
`recipes/<recipe>/artifact_contract.yaml`, while every other recipe-asset read
(workflow.yaml, task_class.yaml, verifier scripts, _synth_artifact_name) honors
MINI_ORK_RECIPE_ROOT - the base main.py threads when a recipe resolves against
the consumer's MINI_ORK_HOME overlay.

Live consequence: the researcher's overlay carried the corrected chapter-review
contract (single-string `source_artifact`, `outputs: []`) but the engine's stale
D-037 copy won. Its list-valued `source_artifact` reached `_envsubst` -> `re.sub`
-> `TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'`, inside a
ProcessPool child whose traceback never reaches the parent. The run then reported
a single failed node, escalated to rollback, and exited non-zero - so the host
runner's `exit_code !== 0` gate discarded a chapter-review whose synthesis and
BOTH verifiers had passed. rubric_status could never flip; every chapter-review
attempt cost $4-6 to fail.

Also align the engine's own chapter-review contract with the shipped design so a
standalone run (no overlay) is not the same landmine.
subject: fix(publisher): resolve artifact_contract via MINI_ORK_RECIPE_ROOT, not the engine root

problem_statement:
fix(researcher): recover lens-<family>.json from stdout when the agent only printed it

The chapter-review lens prompt asks each agent to do two things: emit its score
object on stdout, and write `$MINI_ORK_RUN_DIR/lens-<family>.json` with a tool.
The harness only enforces the first — the researcher handler captures stdout to
`lens-<family>.md` via `_researcher_output_file`, so the `.md` is always
produced, while the `.json` is a model-side coin flip.

Live consequence: in run-1789884609-10608 the kimi and opus lenses printed
their objects and wrote nothing (lens-kimi.md / lens-opus.md are pure JSON, no
.json sibling) while glm wrote the file and printed prose. The panel-completeness
verifier reads `lens-<family>.json` unconditionally, so it failed, the
synthesizer never emitted `chapter-review.json`, and the run was discarded as
`failed_nodes=4` with rubric 2/8 — the chapter's rubric verdict could never
flip on that attempt.

Fix: after the researcher handler persists the agent output, a lens node whose
canonical `.json` is missing or empty recovers the object from the text we
already hold, using the same brace-balanced scanner idiom the repo already uses
in `gates/rubric_scoring.py` and `gates/mutation_adversary.py`. The scanner is
keyed on `"lens"` so recovery stays anchored to the artifact's own shape, and
an existing non-empty sibling always wins.

Fail-soft by design: unparseable output writes nothing and the node still
returns rc 0, so a malformed object degrades to today's behaviour (verifier red)
rather than crashing the node.
subject: fix(researcher): recover lens-<family>.json from stdout when the agent only printed it

problem_statement:
fix(researcher): recover lens-<family>.json from the declared .md too, not just stdout

The lens contract asks each agent to do two things: emit its score object, and
write `$MINI_ORK_RUN_DIR/lens-<family>.json` with a tool. Only the emit is
enforced, so the write is a model-side coin flip — and the shipped recovery
handled just one of its two faces:

  * emitted on stdout, wrote no file  → object is in the stdout we hold;
  * wrote the object into the DECLARED output (lens-<family>.md) with its file
    tool and printed only prose → the stdout has no `{` at all.

`_materialize_lens_json` inspected only the stdout text, so the second shape
produced no `.json`. `recipes/chapter-review/verifiers/panel-completeness.py`
json.loads all four `lens-*.json` unconditionally, so the verifier failed, the
synthesizer never emitted `chapter-review.json`, and the chapter-review was
discarded with the rubric verdict never flipping — ~$4 and ~15 minutes an
attempt, on a chapter that then has to be re-dispatched.

Live consequence, run-1789887625-76705 (ch3 of book d0df3cdb): lens-kimi.md and
lens-opus.md were pure JSON objects, while their .stdout.md siblings were
"Lens emitted. C3=6, C4=5, C8=7…" with zero braces. Both `.json` were missing
and the run was on course to fail panel-completeness.

Fix: when the stdout yields no keyed object, fall back to the declared
lens-<family>.md sibling. `write_preserving_agent` keeps that file only when the
agent wrote it after the dispatch marker, so its presence-as-JSON IS the signal
that the agent used its tool — the same bytes the contract asked for, which we
already hold on disk.

Fail-soft unchanged: an existing non-empty `.json` short-circuits first,
`_first_json_object` still requires a brace-balanced dict carrying a top-level
`"lens"` key, and unparseable output writes nothing and leaves the node at rc 0.
subject: fix(researcher): recover lens-<family>.json from the declared .md too, not just stdout

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): bound the wave subprocess so a hung wave cannot stall the driver

The wave runner spawned `bin/mini-ork run goal-loop <kickoff>` with
`subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True)` and no timeout. On 2026-09-20 a wave
wrote its outputs (sweep-result.json, panel-verdict.json) and then blocked
forever acquiring a lock inside a generator; `subprocess.run` sat on the wave's
pipes, so the driver never advanced to another wave and the whole loop stalled
~47 minutes until the child was killed by hand. The loop's only other bound is
max_waves, which a single hung wave never reaches.

Bound the wave with MO_GOAL_WAVE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 5400 s = the hatchet
executionTimeout ceiling) and fold a timeout as a FAILED wave (exit_code -1,
timed_out true) instead of letting TimeoutExpired escape _default_run_wave_fn.
On POSIX subprocess.run's timeout SIGKILLs and waitpid()s the direct child
without draining the pipes, so a grandchild holding the write end cannot
re-block the driver here. The flag is re-asserted after payload.update(
panel_verdict), so a panel-verdict.json carrying a stale "timed_out": false
cannot mask a wave that actually timed out.

Known limit (deliberate, not fixed here): the wave's own descendants are not
reaped -- subprocess.run kills only the direct child. That matches the manual
recovery this replaces; process-group reaping is a separate change if the leak
ever proves to bite.

Tests: a timing-out wave is reaped and folded as failed without raising; the
env override and the 5400 s default reach subprocess.run; a normal exit keeps
its real code with timed_out false; a stale panel file cannot clobber the
marker; and end-to-end the driver runs wave 2 after wave 1 times out. All six
are red on origin/main's drive.py and green with this fix.
subject: fix(goal-loop): bound the wave subprocess so a hung wave cannot stall the driver

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): scope the fix child's typecheck to its own diff, not the branch

launch-armed.sh sets MO_GOAL_SCOPED_BASE=origin/main, so scoped_gate.py's
`git diff origin/main...HEAD` measured the target worktree's ENTIRE divergence
from main (54 .ts files) rather than the child's change. A child that edited
nothing — the common planner-fallback case — was then typechecked against 44
unrelated files, several of which reference paths absent from that worktree, and
died on pre-existing TS6053 diagnostics. Observed live: "scoped typecheck failed
for 44 changed file(s)" on a child whose implementer reported files_changed: [].

The gate now reads the child's own pre-implementer-ref (its HEAD, or a stash
snapshot of the tree, captured before the first implementer edit) from the run
dir and uses that as the base. Committed work still counts: base...HEAD picks up
any commit the child made on top of it. MO_GOAL_SCOPED_BASE remains the fallback
when there is no run dir, and a non-hex ref value never reaches git.

Verified live against the child that produced the phantom scope: base now
resolves to 6022375b, _changed() returns [], and the gate exits 0 with "no
in-scope TypeScript changes" instead of failing 44 files.
subject: fix(goal-loop): scope the fix child's typecheck to its own diff, not the branch

problem_statement:
fix(rsi): pin the pre-implementer baseline and vendor a pre-edit fixture (E2a)

``_capture_pre_impl_baseline`` snapshotted the pre-edit tree with
``git stash create``, whose commit is reachable from nothing. ``git gc`` reaps
dangling objects, and against the live state.db 22 of 30 failing code runs that
recorded a ref had already lost it. The ref is now pinned to
``refs/mo/pre-impl/<run_id>`` inside the existing best-effort try, so a target
that refuses refs still cannot fail the run.

The second defect was shape, not durability: even a surviving ref pointed at a
whole target repo (the framework itself, or a 230 MB checkout), which is not a
fixture a probe can vendor. ``_capture_pre_impl_fixture`` now writes the changed
files' pre-edit bytes into ``<run_dir>/pre-impl-fixture/``, sourced only from
``git show <baseline>:<relpath>`` — never from model output, since a
model-authored fixture is a model-authored test. Files the implementer created
(new at baseline) get no fixture entry and are recorded under ``created_by_run``.
The capture is idempotent, so a revision loop's second call is a no-op.
subject: fix(rsi): pin the pre-implementer baseline and vendor a pre-edit fixture (E2a)

problem_statement:
fix(observability): restore the node lifecycle feed in dispatch_node

node_events.py had a faithful ported writer (mo_node_start/mo_node_end ->
run_events) with unit tests and zero runtime callers: lib/mo_node_events.sh was
removed in the 2026-07 bash-removal and the port was never wired in. Result:
run_events held 0 rows while runs recorded cost (task_runs=5, llm_calls=63), so
/dag reported never_seen for every node of every run and no consumer of the read
model could see per-node progress.

dispatch_node now emits mo_node_start immediately before the handler and
mo_node_end at the existing trace() completion seam, plus an orphan-close for the
handlers that bypass trace() (verifier/publisher/rollback). mo_node_emit and its
two wrappers take a keyword-only db= that wins over _resolve_db(), because
dispatch_node already holds the run handle and os.environ is not a reliable
carrier mid-run under env isolation. Still fail-silent.

Verified: 3135 unit tests pass; 6 new tests in test_node_event_emission_py.py;
test_mo_node_events_py.py green unmodified. End-to-end, a live dispatch wrote
balanced node_start/node_end rows with correct node_id, node_type, model_lane and
finish_reason, read back by RunDetailRepository.fetch_node_lifecycle_events.
subject: fix(observability): restore the node lifecycle feed in dispatch_node

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): merge the product branch forward on every worker restart

The deploy target is a long-lived branch the loop's children commit onto, so it
drifts behind main, and a fix merged to main is invisible to the worker here
until the branch it actually runs contains it. Measured 2026-09-20: the jina
figure-preservation fix (ba57a71e4) was merged to main, but codex/goalloop-fixes
was 14 commits behind, so every chapter kept losing its figures while the fix
was reported as shipped.

A restart is already the "make the code live" edge, so close the gap there:
before spawning the replacement, merge origin/main (or main) into the target.
The merge is best-effort by construction: a conflict, dirty tree or
unreachable remote aborts the merge and warns, leaving the worktree
byte-identical and never blocking the restart. We refuse to guess at a
conflict resolution (-X ours/theirs), since that would be a fabricated fix; the
conflict is named and left for an operator. MO_GOAL_SYNC_UPSTREAM=0 restores
today's behaviour exactly.

Tests cover the merge-forward, the loop's own commit surviving, a genuine
conflict leaving HEAD and the tree untouched, and the opt-out no-op.
subject: fix(goal-loop): merge the product branch forward on every worker restart

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): stop reading probe detail as predicate axes
