The live PASS reason carries the quality probe's own detail inside the
quality= value:

  ch1 PASS status=completed rubric=pass mdlen=24101 quality=ch1 QUALITY-OK
  sections=4 total=23090 headings=4 [figure-loss attached=8 live=0 ...]

_reason_axes scanned the whole head, so sections/total/headings and the
figure-loss bracket keys were read as axes the predicate had emitted. On the
real book every chapter carries live=0, so the uniform-and-zero rule fired and
the goal met was reported as vacuous with respect to an axis nobody had read
under that name.

Scanning now stops at quality=, the predicate's last axis; everything past it
is the probe's string, not the grammar. The figure-loss bracket is covered by
the same cut and by an explicit test.
subject: fix(goal-loop): stop reading probe detail as predicate axes

problem_statement:
fix(dispatch): an empty home/root must not resolve agents.yaml against the CWD

resolve_lane_family joined "" into the relative path "config/agents.yaml",
which os.path.isfile then resolved against the process CWD. When the repo is
checked out there the lookup silently SUCCEEDS against the repo-default
policy, so a lane alias resolves to a family the run never pinned — codex_lens
to codex, implementer to sonnet. The miss is indistinguishable from a hit
precisely because the wrong file exists.

Guard both joins on a non-empty home/root, so an unset policy is a clean miss
that returns the lane unchanged, and add a ratchet test that fails on the old
behaviour.
subject: fix(dispatch): an empty home/root must not resolve agents.yaml against the CWD

problem_statement:
fix(rubric): budget artifact_summary by size and label every cut

The rubric grader is handed artifact_summary(run_dir) via
{{DIFF_SUMMARY}}, and every text artifact was clipped to its first 25
lines with no marker. A 43-line synthesis was therefore shown ending
mid-section with nothing saying it had been cut, so the grader failed
it on checklist item 8 ("no truncation") and could not grade goal /
artifacts-complete against content it was never shown. The 25-line cap
also bit far below the budget: a 505-byte file was cut to 27% of itself
while 11KB of the 12KB budget sat unused.

Budget the summary instead of clipping each file:

- Reserve headers first, so a starved budget still lists what exists.
- Give every text file a foothold (_MIN_FILE_CHARS, or its whole content
  when smaller), then share the surplus in proportion to remaining size.
- Hand slack from files that fit in full to the largest still-cut ones.
- Cut on line boundaries, and always append an exact
  "N of M lines, B of S bytes shown" label. The label is charged
  against the file's own share so the global cap cannot clip it.

A run dir's headline artifact is normally its biggest, so it now takes
most of the budget rather than whichever file sorts first.

Tests cover the original 43-line repro, the crowded-run-dir case, and
that the label's counts match the file; all three fail against the
prior implementation. The module docstrings that claimed byte-parity
with the retired bash twin are corrected -- this function diverged.
subject: fix(rubric): budget artifact_summary by size and label every cut

problem_statement:
fix(ucci): window the calibration fit to recent rows

The module docstring claimed the map was refit from recent rows rather
than fitted once, but load_margin_rows selected every row for the
task_class, unbounded. A lane whose model or prompt changed kept
calibrating against its pre-change history, so the threshold described a
lane that no longer exists.

Enforce the claim: a recency window (MO_UCCI_WINDOW_DAYS, default 30d)
and a per-slice row cap (MO_UCCI_MAX_ROWS, default 500, newest first).
Both clamp one-directionally from the environment, like target_error and
min_samples: the env can shorten the window and lower the cap, never the
reverse.

The cutoff is built in execution_traces.created_at's own format
(%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ). SQLite's datetime('now','-N days') emits a space
separator that sorts below every T-formatted row on the same day and
would admit an extra day of stale rows.

No change to pav, fit_error_map or error_probability: the algorithmic
surface is untouched, so the reference implementation's golden vectors
still pin this port.

calibration_backtest.load_prediction_rows is deliberately left
unwindowed: the check ON the fit must read all history for drift to
surface as a rising ECE. Recorded in its docstring.
subject: fix(ucci): window the calibration fit to recent rows

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): give the deploy resync a git identity

The restart binding's `_sync_upstream` merges the product branch into the
deploy target with `git merge --no-edit`. A merge writes a commit, so on a
runner with no configured identity git dies with `empty ident name ... not
allowed` — the state every CI runner and fresh container starts in. The
binding reports any failed merge as `merge conflict against main`, so the
deploy target silently stopped carrying the product branch forward, which is
exactly the regression this binding exists to prevent: the book worker kept
running a branch 14 commits behind while the fix it needed was reported as
shipped.

Supply the project-wide fallback identity (`mini-ork` / `mini-ork@localhost`,
matching `vcs/rebase_guard.py` and `vcs/auto_merge.py`) and apply it only to
the mutating merge call, leaving other git invocations on the inherited env.
A configured identity still wins, and an explicitly empty one is filled too —
that empty-variable case is what CI actually presents.

The new test empties the four `GIT_*` variables and points both config files
at the null device so git has no name to write, which reproduces the failure
on macOS as well as Linux; without the fix it reports the same
`merge conflict against main (fatal: empty ident name ...)` CI saw.
subject: fix(goal-loop): give the deploy resync a git identity

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): a failed merge is not always a conflict

`_sync_upstream` returned `merge conflict against {ref} (...)` for every
non-zero merge, and warned "resolve by hand" with the last line of git's
stderr pasted in as if it named conflicted paths. Only a merge that stops on
content leaves conflicted paths (`diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`); a merge
refused before it starts — no git identity, a held lock, a refusing hook,
local changes it would overwrite — leaves none, and there is nothing for an
operator to resolve.

That mislabelling is what let the missing-identity bug go unnoticed: the
deploy target quietly stopped carrying main forward while the warning said
"conflict", a shape that reads as ordinary and expected. Split the two: keep
"merge conflict against {ref}" only when paths are actually conflicted, and
otherwise return "merge failed against {ref} (no conflicted paths: ...)" with
git's own reason, which is the whole diagnostic.
subject: fix(goal-loop): a failed merge is not always a conflict

problem_statement:
fix(trace-store): fail open on schema drift instead of killing the trace write

The live DB had route_margin (0057) but not predicted_error (0059), because
0059 was never applied — and trace_write named predicted_error unconditionally.
Every write raised OperationalError and execute.py swallowed it as best-effort,
so the ledger froze at 2026-09-23T10:10:46 and nothing surfaced it. Zero route
margins read as "UCCI is unused" when it was a write-path outage.

The writer now reads PRAGMA table_info once and drops any column the table
lacks from both the INSERT list and the ON CONFLICT clause, so a lagging schema
degrades to a narrower write rather than raising. Columns are declared in one
_TRACE_COLUMNS table carrying each column's conflict mode (skip/set/coalesce),
which also removes the three-place edit hazard the route-provenance tests were
written to police. Coercion is unchanged; the existing row-shape tests pass
untouched.

A missing TABLE still raises — fail-open is for column drift, not a wrong DB
path.
subject: fix(trace-store): fail open on schema drift instead of killing the trace write

problem_statement:
fix: derive framework-edit's diff from the tree, and implement the in-place rollback strategy (#207)

* fix(framework-edit): derive the implementer diff from the tree, not the agent's claim

framework-edit's implementer writes framework-edit.diff itself and nothing
validated that artifact against reality. A hallucinating agent emitted a
corrupt diff — garbage hunk context, already-landed files re-declared as new
creations — AND fabricated its verification claims ("git apply --check ->
EXIT=0"), so the run burned the whole verifier+reviewer wave before the lie
surfaced. The working tree is the only witness that cannot lie.

After apply_impl_output, re-derive the delta from git and rewrite
framework-edit.diff from it: the artifact then always applies, the static
gate's reverse-check is trivially true, and the dispatcher's landing is exact.

The baseline is captured before the first implementer iteration
(_capture_pre_impl_baseline), so a concurrent session's uncommitted work is
never swept into this run's diff. `git stash create` snapshots TRACKED state
only, so the untracked inventory is recorded alongside it — without that,
every pre-existing untracked file (another session's scratch file, a
node_modules symlink) would be re-declared as implementer-created and
published as part of the fix.

A diff-only agent stays legitimate: when the tree is untouched and the
artifact applies cleanly, it is applied once and the tree becomes the source
again. When neither yields anything the implementer node fails immediately
with impl_no_changes / impl_diff_unusable rather than five nodes later, and
the agent's artifact is preserved as framework-edit.diff.agent so the lie
stays auditable.

The tests run against real temp git repos and each one was falsified by
re-breaking its mechanism (dropping the untracked-baseline filter, the
.mini-ork/ skip, the empty-delta guard, and the delegate registration).

* fix(rollback): implement keep_run_artifacts_discard_worktree for in-place runs

Both recipes/framework-edit/workflow.yaml and recipes/self-migrate/workflow.yaml
declare `rollback_strategy: keep_run_artifacts_discard_worktree`, and the
strategy was implemented nowhere — only revert_branch was. A failed in-place run
therefore left the harvested diff sitting in the target tree (a preflight against
run-1788363267-21773-se1 found 4 staged paths behind), so the next serial epic
started from a dirty base and its reviewer diff swept in the dead run's work.

_revert_inplace_diff reverses the run's own framework-edit.diff. The in-place
agent may leave any mix of states, so the restore is per-path and
state-agnostic: `git checkout HEAD -- <path>` resets index AND worktree for
paths in HEAD, while created paths are unstaged and unlinked — `git apply -R`
alone reverts worktree content but leaves the agent's staged entries behind.
Paths outside the diff are never touched, and the containment check keeps a
traversing diff path from reaching outside MO_TARGET_CWD. Run artifacts (diff,
verdicts, logs) survive, per the strategy's name.

MINI_ORK_ROLLBACK_KEEP_WORKTREE is hoisted so it covers both strategies. It is
the outer-loop escape hatch: in a closed RSI loop the authoritative gate is
downstream (deploy -> regen -> DB flip) and it tests the FILE state the
implementer produced, so an in-sandbox revert would destroy a verified-correct
edit before the real gate ever sees it. Leaving the flag wired to revert_branch
alone would have newly destroyed exactly those edits, so the check moved above
the strategy dispatch and the in-place branch honours it too.

* feat(config): add MINI_ORK_AGENTS, and honour MINI_ORK_PROVIDERS everywhere

A vendored mini-ork checkout is a pure mirror of upstream: re-vendoring RESETS
it. So a consumer that configures the engine by editing
$MINI_ORK_HOME/config/{providers,agents}.yaml inside the checkout loses that
configuration on every re-vendor, silently — the files are tracked, and
`reset --hard` restores the upstream defaults with no error. Both files hold
lane policy (model, provider, cost), so the loss is invisible until the wrong
model bills.

MINI_ORK_PROVIDERS already existed as a path override in dispatch/providers.py,
but three other readers of the same files ignored it, so the engine could
resolve lanes from one file while validating, profiling, and gating against
another. Honour it in the validate secrets check, and add the matching
MINI_ORK_AGENTS seam for agents.yaml in the profile step and the coalition
gate. Both are documented in the CLI help next to MINI_ORK_PROVIDERS.

web/recipes.py:load_lanes is deliberately not wired to MINI_ORK_AGENTS: it
already takes an explicit `home` parameter rather than joining a hardcoded
path, so callers can already point it at the consumer's config.

* test(recovery): give the closure-filter test a real edit surface

`test_execute_loop_dispatches_only_closure` ran a four-node synthetic
workflow whose nodes are all `implementer`, under MINI_ORK_RECIPE=
framework-edit, with a mock LLM that writes nothing and no MO_TARGET_CWD.
Then it asserted rc == 0. That expectation is exactly the behaviour the
ground-truth harvest exists to forbid: a framework-edit implementer that
changes no file now fails the node with `impl_no_changes` instead of
falling through to the verifiers.

The fixture is what was unrealistic, not the guard. The real
recipes/framework-edit/workflow.yaml has one implementer and it edits the
target tree by definition; this test's all-implementer shape is a device to
avoid verdict.json gating, and its own comment already says the closure
filter under test is node-shape agnostic.

So: create a scratch git repo, point MO_TARGET_CWD at it, and have the mock
implementer write its edit there — an in-place implementer edits
MO_TARGET_CWD directly. Node identity still comes from MO_NODE_ID, so
`seen == ["D"]`, the assertion this test exists for, is untouched.

MO_TARGET_CWD is set with monkeypatch rather than the raw os.environ the
neighbouring lines use: the surrounding vars leak past teardown, and a
leaked MO_TARGET_CWD would silently retarget a later test's harvest.

Falsified: with the mock's file-write removed the test fails again with
`[ground-truth] FAIL: implementer produced no tree changes`. Before the fix
the harvest also fell back to the mini-ork checkout itself (the `[cwd] codex
target:` line named it), so the test was reading the wrong tree entirely.

tests/ -q --ignore=tests/unit: 398 passed, 24 skipped. Ruff clean.
subject: fix: derive framework-edit's diff from the tree, and implement the in-place rollback strategy (#207)

problem_statement:
fix(cost): meter real spend, and stop one dispatch's cost landing on many traces

Two defects kept the ledger from matching reality.

The daily budget guard summed task_runs.cost_usd, which only carries what a
node handler explicitly charged. Stage spend (reflect / gradient-extract, the
jury, the lens panel) never reaches a charge call, so the guard read $0.00
against $3.1302 of real dispatch spend in the last 24h and the
MO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD circuit could not fire. today_cost_usd now sums llm_calls —
the per-dispatch ledger every provider call writes, node or stage — and falls
back to the task_runs sum when llm_calls is absent, so a DB behind the migrator
degrades to the old estimate rather than to a blind zero.

Separately, the .last-llm-* sidecars are overwritten per dispatch and never
consumed, so a node that dispatched nothing read the previous node's cost back
as its own: four traces per smoke run carried the same $0.177876 while three of
the four were transform nodes that never dispatched. Dispatchers now stamp
.last-llm-node with MO_NODE_ID and clear the sidecars before writing, and
_read_fresh_sidecar returns None when the stamp and the current node disagree.
A writer that stamps no node stays trusted on freshness alone, so the gate
narrows attribution without being able to blank it out.

The node gate also lets trace_write overlay the RESOLVED lane: agent_version_id
arrives as the lane the router was asked for, which may be a two-element retry
family — `glm,minimax` is a legitimate value there, and it held an advantage row
competing with its own members for the same slice. Only the member the
dispatcher actually served is now credited.
subject: fix(cost): meter real spend, and stop one dispatch's cost landing on many traces

problem_statement:
fix(run-dir): stop a dry run's artifacts shadowing the live run's record

A run dir must record the live run, but two first-writer-wins guards let a
rehearsal that shared the run id win instead.

`_emit_run_verdict` returned early whenever an existing `verdict.json` carried
`source: execute@run-level`. A nested lifecycle that inherits `MINI_ORK_RUN_ID`
(a DRY_RUN rehearsal of a different recipe — the class `probe_scorer` already
strips) wrote that file first, so the live emit skipped and the run dir kept a
rehearsal's verdict as the run's outcome. Rehearsals now write
`verdict.dryrun.json`, which also means they no longer test the
`panel-verdict.json` guard that exists to protect the live run.

`_run_lifecycle_impl` wrote `execute.log` only `if not isfile`, so a rehearsal's
log likewise became the run's log. The write now targets
`execute.dryrun.log` under `MINI_ORK_DRY_RUN=1`, and the `isfile` guard is gone:
the live run is the only author of its own log, so nothing should pre-empt it.

Observed on a goal-loop child whose 8-node code-fix run (3 failed nodes,
reviewer needs_revision) left behind a 5-node docs-recipe dry-run's
`execute.log` and `verdict.json` as the run's evidence.

Tests: tests/unit/test_dryrun_artifact_shadowing_py.py covers the ordering that
corrupted that child (rehearsal first, live second), verdict idempotency, the
recipe-owned-verdict fallback, and both log names. 3479 unit tests pass.
subject: fix(run-dir): stop a dry run's artifacts shadowing the live run's record

problem_statement:
fix(plan): stop a dry run's plan from overwriting the live run's own plan

mini_ork/cli/plan.py wrote `_DRY_RUN_PLACEHOLDER` to `<run>/plan.json` — the
live run's own filename — so a rehearsal that had inherited `MINI_ORK_RUN_ID`
left the live run's plan reading `objective: '<dry-run: not generated>'` with an
empty decomposition. Every node downstream was then executed and reviewed
against a null objective.

Evidence: `.mini-ork/runs/child-1790350588-96925` held a live code-fix lifecycle
(8 nodes, `execute.log`, `verdict.json` fail) *and* a dry-run docs rehearsal (5
nodes, `execute.dryrun.log`, `verdict.dryrun.json` pass). `plan.json` held the
placeholder, and the reviewer recorded it verbatim: "Plan is a dry-run shell:
objective='<dry-run: not generated>', decomposition=[], run_profile
.profile_status='needs_answers' ... no real objective existed to implement or
review against."

This is the same defect adfa44d0 fixed for `execute.log` and `verdict.json`, one
stage earlier — and the stage that matters, since the plan is the artifact the
implementer and reviewer actually consume. `_plan_file_name()` mirrors
`main._execute_log_name()`; an explicit `--out` is not routed through it, so a
caller that names the file keeps it.

Tests (tests/unit/test_dryrun_artifact_shadowing_py.py, +4 cases): the naming
contract, a rehearsal landing on `plan.dryrun.json` and never on `plan.json`,
the rehearsal-then-live sequence leaving the live plan intact, and `--out`
honoured verbatim. The two behavioural cases were falsified first — reverting
the mechanism to `"plan.json"` reddens both, and only both.
subject: fix(plan): stop a dry run's plan from overwriting the live run's own plan

problem_statement:
fix(cli): pin the engine for module children so a cwd cannot shadow it

A `python -m mini_ork.cli.*` child puts the working directory at
sys.path[0], ahead of the PYTHONPATH that names the engine. The goal-loop
runs a child with its cwd set to the repo under repair, so a repo that
contains a mini_ork/ tree silently shadowed the engine: the plan child
executed the target's stale copy, which wrote the rehearsal placeholder
over the live run's own plan.json. Every child was then planned against
objective "<dry-run: not generated>" with an empty decomposition, which is
why a fix merged to main stayed inert inside the running loop.

PYTHONSAFEPATH drops the implicit cwd entry so the declared PYTHONPATH
resolves. The plan child's hand-built env is replaced by the shared helper
so it cannot drift from every other module child.
subject: fix(cli): pin the engine for module children so a cwd cannot shadow it

problem_statement:
fix(goal-loop): a wave that measured nothing is not a green wave

The self-campaign ran two waves, spent $13.51 of its $150 budget, and
stopped with `regressing:0->3` — killing a loop that was working. The
cause was the fold, not the loop: wave 1 timed out before writing
`panel-verdict.json`, `_default_run_wave_fn` defaulted the missing
`failing_units` to `[]`, and an unobserved empty set is byte-identical
to a measured "nothing failing". Wave 2's honest count of three then
read as a regression from zero, and `divergence` fired.

The distinction the fold could not make is now carried explicitly. A
wave whose verdict names no failing set records `verdict_known: False`:
no signature (the hash of the empty set is exactly what a satisfied
goal hashes to), no headroom, no predicate_moved, and no fix-hash
sighting — so a timeout can no longer read as "attempted twice, same
failure" and quarantine a unit the loop never scored.

Every detector that reasons about the failing set reads the measured
tail instead of the raw wave list. The cut is a BREAK, not a filter:
divergence is `patience` CONSECUTIVE waves, so an unobserved wave
between two measured ones means the pattern was not sustained across
it. Silence there is the absence of evidence, not evidence of progress.

The flag is additive — absent means measured, so every existing state
file and every caller that does not know about it behaves as before. A
real pass still writes `failing_units: []`, still carries the empty-set
signature, and still stops `goal_met`. Stop reports name what the loop
last OBSERVED (`failing_now`), and the waves that produced no
measurement ride out as `unmeasured_waves`.

Also unlinks `panel-verdict.json` before each wave's subprocess: the
file lives in the shared run dir and was never cleared, so a wave that
died would have been scored on the previous wave's verdict.

The regression test replays the live failure — a wave with no failing
key followed by a measured three — and fails on the old code with the
campaign's exact signature, `regressing:0->3`.
subject: fix(goal-loop): a wave that measured nothing is not a green wave

problem_statement:
fix(rollback): restore in-place paths to the pre-run snapshot, not HEAD (#208)

Review of #208 found the in-place rollback could destroy work that was
never this run's:

- A path a concurrent session had already dirtied was reset with
  `checkout HEAD`, wiping that session's uncommitted edit along with the
  implementer's. Pre-dirty paths are now restored from the
  pre-implementer-ref snapshot, and only the agent's staging is dropped.
- A move was never reverted: `git diff` detects renames by default and
  `git apply --numstat` names only the destination, so rollback deleted
  the new file and left the source missing. The harvest now diffs with
  --no-renames, and rollback also reads `rename from` lines for
  agent-written diffs.
- The baseline was captured on the first dispatch of ANY node, so a
  rollback that ran first in a run dir snapshotted the already-edited tree
  and restored to it. Rollback nodes no longer capture the baseline.

Harvest hardening:
- `ls-files -z`, so non-ASCII untracked names are not C-quoted and
  silently dropped.
- surrogateescape decoding, so a non-UTF-8 byte round-trips into the diff
  instead of raising and falling back to the agent's artifact.
- A baseline that is not a commit in the harvested tree is reported
  explicitly instead of as a generic "git diff failed".

Known limit, now documented in the docstring: an edit another session
makes to the SAME path while the implementer runs cannot be told apart
from the implementer's, and is discarded with it.

Six new tests; each fails on the previous commit and passes here.
tests/ --ignore=tests/unit: 398 passed, 24 skipped.
subject: fix(rollback): restore in-place paths to the pre-run snapshot, not HEAD (#208)

problem_statement:
fix(router): keep the z-score on the UCB bonus's scale

Live state.db, goal_loop/implementer/code-delivery: every lane's z was
about -900, so the UCB exploration bonus (<~1.1) could never reorder
lanes and the router locked onto codex on the strength of one run.

Two bugs compounded:
- The slice baseline divided its weighted moments by the GROUP count, so
  slice_mean was a sum of scores and slice_var was sum(x^2) - sum(x)^2,
  negative and clamped to 0. Divide by the summed run weight instead.
- _zscore subtracted that raw-score mean from an advantage that is
  already group-relative, then divided by a 1e-3 floor. It now divides
  the advantage by max(slice std, MO_ROUTER_Z_STD_FLOOR), default 0.1.

On a copy of the live DB the goal_loop z-scores move from
[-922, -899] to [-0.46, +0.31].

Existing lane_slice_baseline rows still hold the old values and are
blended in by the EMA (alpha 0.30); the floor covers them until they
decay.
subject: fix(router): keep the z-score on the UCB bonus's scale

problem_statement:
fix(router): runs_count counts runs, not GRPO groups

recompute_advantages persisted the number of GRPO groups a lane appeared
in as runs_count. Groups are keyed by code region, so:

- every lane_region_advantage row was pinned at runs_count=1, below the
  default MO_LEARNING_MIN_SAMPLES=3 — the region routing level was
  unreachable by construction;
- domain rows counted code regions touched, so the sample floor and the
  UCB bonus's n measured breadth, not evidence.

On the live DB this left goal_loop/implementer with ONE eligible lane —
minimax, the lowest advantage (-0.046) — so the router sent goal-loop
work to its weakest lane.

runs_count now sums the lane's runs across the groups that produced its
advantage. "groups" still divides the advantage average, so advantages
are unchanged. On a copy of the live DB: 50/84 domain rows and 31/52
region rows clear the floor (was 4 and 0); goal_loop picks glm,minimax.

test_recompute_advantage / test_preferred_lane pinned the old group
count (1 per lane) and are updated to the run count (3).
subject: fix(router): runs_count counts runs, not GRPO groups

problem_statement:
fix(certify): run the model lane in a throwaway dir, never the user's repo

Agentic lanes have file tools and run in MO_TARGET_CWD, else the process
cwd. During a live certify a lane recreated the package under test in the
caller's cwd to try its probe. certify runs inside the user's own repo, so
each call now gets a scratch MO_TARGET_CWD (via scoped_environ) that is
removed afterwards. Live re-check without MO_ALLOW_FRAMEWORK_CWD: correct
fix PROVEN, cheat REFUTED, both repos left clean.
subject: fix(certify): run the model lane in a throwaway dir, never the user's repo

problem_statement:
fix(recover): CLI dispatches the closure it prints, then frees the run

`mini-ork recover` spawns the planner module in its own process, so main()'s
env hand-off never reached an executor: it printed "dispatching closure",
returned 0 without running a node, and held the run lease for its TTL.
cli_main() now runs execute --recovery in-process on the planned closure,
closes the recovery request (completed|failed) and releases the lease.
The recipe falls back to run_profile.json so a CLI recover no longer hashes
every checkpoint as recipe=unknown (all hash_mismatch).
subject: fix(recover): CLI dispatches the closure it prints, then frees the run

problem_statement:
fix(dispatch): attribute lane failures to their real cause

Three defects compounded so that one failed reviewer call surfaced as an
unrelated error on a different node:

- core: a non-zero harness exit recorded stderr only. The Claude CLI in
  JSON mode puts the API error in its stdout result envelope
  (is_error, api_error_status, result) and may print only an advisory
  banner on stderr, so a 403 "Key limit exceeded" was logged as the
  banner. Lead with the envelope message; keep the stderr tail after it.

- routing: with no state DB, learning_static_lane forced every unpinned
  reviewer to MO_FRONTIER_LANE (and researcher/implementer to
  MO_CHEAP_LANE), overriding an operator's agents.yaml `lanes.<role>`
  mapping - often set precisely to avoid the frontier default. Keep the
  role when it is mapped; the defaults now fill unmapped roles only.

- rollback/verify: the post-run verify runs after rollback and reported
  files rollback itself deleted as "required artifact missing or empty",
  blaming the implementer. revert_branch now records reverted paths in
  <run_dir>/rolled-back.json and verify labels them detail=rolled_back.
  The verdict is unchanged: a reverted run still fails.
subject: fix(dispatch): attribute lane failures to their real cause

problem_statement:
fix(routing): explicit lane knobs outrank the agents.yaml role mapping

Review of #209. Letting a mapped agents.yaml role win over everything
disabled static_hybrid: the shipped agents.yaml maps planner, researcher,
implementer and reviewer, so the mapped-role check always fired,
MO_FRONTIER_LANE / MO_CHEAP_LANE were silently ignored, and the policy
became identical to workflow_default. learning_governed inherited the
same fallback.

Precedence for an unpinned role is now: recipe pin > explicitly set
MO_FRONTIER_LANE / MO_CHEAP_LANE > agents.yaml mapping > built-in
defaults. The incident this PR fixes (reviewer mapped away from a capped
frontier key, no env knob set) still resolves through the mapping.

Also record rolled-back.json from the in-place rollback
(keep_run_artifacts_discard_worktree), which framework-edit and
self-migrate use; only revert_branch wrote it, so those recipes still
reported reverted artifacts as "missing or empty".

Both new tests fail on d7c5c689 and pass here.
subject: fix(routing): explicit lane knobs outrank the agents.yaml role mapping
